title: Smoked Brisket BBQ Pizza
seoTitle: Smoked Brisket BBQ Pizza | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Leftover brisket, tangy sauce
description: Leftover brisket, tangy sauce. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Warm and chop brisket
steps.instruction: Chop cooked brisket into small cubes; toss with a few tablespoons BBQ sauce and vinegar. Warm gently in a skillet — cold brisket drops the oven temp and steams the pie.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 500°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 500°F at least 40 minutes. This pie uses leftover smoked brisket; you are not smoking meat tonight.

steps.title: Stretch rounds and BBQ base
steps.instruction: Stretch four 12–14 inch rounds. Spread a thin layer of BBQ sauce — less than a saucy sandwich. Brush rims with oil.

steps.title: Cheese, brisket, onion
steps.instruction: Layer mozzarella and gouda, then brisket and red onion. Pickled jalapeños if your hall likes heat. Do not pile brisket an inch thick or the center never crisps.

steps.title: Bake until cheese spots brown
steps.instruction: Bake 10–13 minutes until cheese browns and crust sounds hollow. Brisket is cooked; focus on crust and cheese set. Rotate once.

steps.title: Slaw on top, rest, and cut
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes. Top with cold coleslaw in the center of each pie or serve slaw on the side — hot slaw wilts. Cut 8 slices. Smoked Brisket BBQ Pizza is hall BBQ night on a crust.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Smoked Brisket BBQ Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Leftover brisket, tangy sauce. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
